text:
incident-bot: ALERT: unusual traffic pattern detected -> /v1/embeddings spike 14.8k req/min (fanout). Auto-safeguards flagged 503s & token errors, creating incident thread 6032109999.
oncall-ryan: ack, I'm on it. Seeing global spike, concentrating on eu-west and us-east edges.
sre-amber: confirmed 429/503 increase starting +6m. KV cache miss rate up 3x, tail latency rising.
support-jess: multiple customers (acct:cobalt, acct-zeno) reporting failed batch jobs, support queue heating.
devops-lee: proposing immediate soft quota freeze for new API keys + slice embeddings to 30% for anonymous tier. Can push in 2 mins.
sec-ops: recommend WAF JS challenge + block list for obvious crawler IP ranges. Will assemble list and hand to lee.
oncall-ryan: do both. Order of ops: 1) slice anonymous/guest traffic 2) enable JS challenge on WAF for suspicious UA 3) circuit-break long-running embedding batches 4) notify support.
devops-lee: running command now: ```rdctl limits set --route "/v1/embeddings" --policy slice --percent 30 --scope "anonymous" --note "abuse spike 6032109999"```
devops-lee: slice applied. telemetry shows immediate inbound reduction ~28%.
sre-amber: applying a temporary circuit-break for requests >60s to avoid inflight build-up. Patching rollout.
sec-ops: WAF rule ready. Rule id=waf-6032-js-challenge. Targets UA regex: (curl|python-requests|node-fetch) and IP ranges listed in paste. Applying to eu-west/us-east edges.
sec-ops: WAF rule applied -> initial drop ~22% of offending requests.
support-jess: drafting customer comms: "We're seeing anomalous scraper activity affecting embeddings batching for some customers. We've applied mitigations; if you see errors, please open ticket. ETA for monitoring: 2h." Want signoff.
product-maya: +1 to comms. Keep it concise and avoid revealing internal throttles. Suggest include mitigation steps customers can take (reduce batch size, retry/backoff).
oncall-ryan: customer comms approved. Jess, please send via support channel and email template C-embeds-1.
support-jess: will send now.
devops-lee: noticed one internal job from acct:delta still spiking due to pinned dedicated IPs. Temporarily disabled batch endpoint for that tenant: ```rdctl endpoint disable --tenant delta --endpoint embeddings-batch```
sre-amber: good call. That reduced per-VM memory pressure. KV cache stalls declining.
sec-ops: adding 403 block for 12 IP ranges tied to known botnet. Saving logs for forensics.
oncall-ryan: create a short incident summary and add to JIRA: INF-9453. Include actions taken and links to metrics/dashboards.
devops-lee: INF-9453 created. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-9453
support-jess: support note sent to affected customers, thread: https://redwood.support/threads/4182. Ticket numbers attached.
oncall-ryan: handing off to oncall-maria for follow-up and overnight watch. Key items for handoff: - WAF rule waf-6032 active - Anonymous slice 30% - Delta tenant batch endpoint disabled - Alerts set on 5xx/429 and kvcache-miss - JIRA INF-9453 - Support comms live
oncall-maria: ack. I'll take over monitoring. My plan: keep WAF rule for 2 hours, then soft rollback if stable; keep quota slice until throughput normalizes; keep delta disabled until they finish investigating.
sre-amber: leaving a quick runbook snippet for Maria: ```if tail latency > 1.5s or 5xx rate > 2% over 5m -> increment slice to 20% (anonymous), escalate to infra lead; if kvcache miss > 5% -> enable extra kvcache nodes (infractl kvcache scale +2).```
oncall-maria: got it. I'll also bump on-call paging thresholds to be more sensitive and follow up with sec-ops for IP takedown request.
support-jess: I'll continue customer follow-ups and mark impacted tickets as incident-related.
product-maya: log customer impact for billing/SLAs. We may offer credit if jobs delayed > 2 hours.
oncall-maria: thanks everyone. I'll post a short post-incident summary in #incidents after 4h assessment. Leaving thread open.
